title: One data lake module, two teams
skills: module outputs in the root module

ticket.subject: Marketing wants the same lake as sales: no copy-paste
body: Marketing needs a data lake exactly like the sales one. Instead of copying fifty lines of HCL per team, Tom
started a module in `modules/datalake/` before his holiday: `variables.tf` is done, `main.tf` is a draft that
was never applied. Please finish the module and call it once per team from the root module (`main.tf`).
and the `team` input set. The root module declares no resource itself: everything goes through the module.
- **One lake per team**: resource group `rg-<team>-lake-dev`, ADLS Gen2 storage account `st<team>lakedev01`
(storage account names are unique across all of Azure: two teams cannot share one), and one container per
zone of `var.zones` from a single `for_each` block `azurerm_storage_container.zone`.
- **Tags**: every resource gets `cost_center = "CC-4410"` and `env = "dev"` from the root module, plus
- **Outputs**: the root module outputs `sales_dfs_endpoint` and `marketing_dfs_endpoint`, read from a
- **CI**: our pipeline runs `terraform fmt -check -recursive` and fails on any file it lists. Tom's draft would
fail it. Run it yourself and fix the layout in the editor (the lab never rewrites your files).
When you are done, `terraform plan` must say there is nothing left to change.
This is the lab's simulated subscription: nothing is created in Azure.

acceptance.text: The root module calls ./modules/datalake twice, sales and marketing, and declares no resource itself.

checks.fail: The root module does not call the module as the ticket asks.
The containers are not one for_each block over var.zones in the module.

acceptance.text: Each team has its own resource group, ADLS Gen2 account and three zone containers.

checks.fail: The sales lake is not as the ticket describes.

The applied containers are not the three zones of each lake.

hints: A module is a folder of .tf files. `module "sales" { source = "./modules/datalake"  team = "sales" }` calls it; every other argument of the block sets one of its variables. Run `terraform init` again after adding a module call: Terraform installs modules at init.

Inside the module, resources are addressed without the module prefix (`azurerm_storage_account.this`); from outside they are `module.sales.azurerm_storage_account.this`, which is what `terraform state list` shows.
The root module cannot read a module's resources directly: the module must declare `output "dfs_endpoint"`, and the root reads `module.sales.dfs_endpoint`.
A hard-coded storage account name works for the first team and fails for the second: the name is unique across all of Azure. Build it from `var.team` and `var.env`.
`terraform fmt -check -recursive` lists the files whose layout differs; add `-diff` to see what to change: two-space indentation and the `=` of consecutive arguments aligned.
`merge(var.tags, { team = var.team })` in a `locals` block of the module adds the team tag to what the root passes.
